external_entities.name: calling service
external_entities.description: A backend operated by another team that calls the inference gateway.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
external_entities.notes: The source refers to multiple calling services but does not distinguish them, so they are represented as one entity.

external_entities.name: ML engineer
external_entities.description: An ML engineer who publishes model artifacts to the registry bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
external_entities.notes: unknown what governs who can push; the source says it may be a shared group account.

processes.name: inference gateway
processes.description: A FastAPI service that receives inference requests from calling backends and forwards them to the model server, while logging requests and responses.
processes.source_excerpt: our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE
processes.notes: Callers pass an API key in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and have never expired.

processes.name: model server
processes.description: The model-serving process running the actual model on GPU nodes and reading model artifacts and customer features.
processes.source_excerpt: the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network
processes.notes: It uses its own service account to load model artifacts. The source does not establish whether artifact integrity is verified.

data_stores.name: model registry bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket containing model artifacts loaded by the model server at startup.
data_stores.source_excerpt: model artifacts from a model registry bucket
data_stores.notes: The source says the bucket is trusted and does not say that artifact integrity is verified.

data_stores.name: Redis feature store
data_stores.description: A Redis store containing customer features including account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Redis feature store on the same network
data_stores.notes: Redis has no password and is only reachable inside the model network.

data_stores.name: inference log
data_stores.description: A BigQuery log containing every inference request and response for debugging, including raw prompts that may contain user-entered text.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_stores.notes: Raw prompts sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: submit inference
data_flows.description: A calling service submits an inference request to the internet-exposed gateway, including an API key in a header.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Callers pass an API key in a header.
data_flows.notes: Keys are issued per calling team and have never expired.

data_flows.name: forward request
data_flows.description: The gateway forwards an inference request to the model server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway forwards the request to the model server
data_flows.notes: There is no authentication between the gateway and the model server.

data_flows.name: load artifacts
data_flows.description: The model server loads model artifacts from the registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.notes: The model server uses its own service account. The source says, 'I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket.'

data_flows.name: read features
data_flows.description: The model server reads customer features from the Redis feature store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the model server reads from a Redis feature store
data_flows.data_description: Customer features including account age and spend bands per customer

data_flows.name: write log
data_flows.description: The gateway writes every inference request and response to the BigQuery inference log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_flows.notes: The logged data includes raw prompts that sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.
data_flows.data_description: Inference requests and responses, including raw prompts

data_flows.name: publish artifacts
data_flows.description: An ML engineer publishes new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source is unsure what governs who can push and thinks it may be a shared group account.

trust_boundaries.name: model network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the model server and Redis feature store.
trust_boundaries.notes: The model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway.

trust_boundaries.name: different cloud
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud containing two of the calling services.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: two of the calling services are in a different cloud
trust_boundaries.notes: The source identifies a different cloud but does not identify its operator or authority level.

assumptions.assumption: The different cloud is a distinct network trust boundary for the calling service.
assumptions.basis: The source states that two calling services are in a different cloud, which describes a distinct network location.

assumptions.assumption: The Redis feature store's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It contains customer features including account age and spend bands per customer.

assumptions.assumption: The inference log's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It contains raw prompts that sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed, which may contain information about people or the business.
